state:
Goal `core-str-3-3`: `upper` and `upperFirst` now have every feature proof on disk: description,
three examples each, an attack each, a bench record, a Rust test carrying their `covers:` markers,
and cards in plain words. `upper` used to build a Rust `String` before its result, and the memory
limit never saw that buffer. `ΐ` triples in bytes, so it could reach about four times the input.
`upper` now writes straight into the result, which asks the limit before each growth.
`upperFirst`/`lowerFirst` are one allocation of exact length. The `lower`/`lowerFirst` benches only
ever measured one or two of their three words, and are fixed. `benches/members/README.md` § *Chain
the inputs* now says why. Every `Core\Str` perf record was re-measured after `str.rs` changed. The
only member this goal still owes is `wrap`.

items.text: **`Core\Str::wrap`** — owes about, examples, hostile, perf, tests (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). Its result can be much longer than its input (a width of 1 adds a break after every character, and `break` can be long), so check that `wrapped` asks the memory limit before it grows its `String`, the way `upper` now writes through `built`. Attack it with a width of 1 and a long `break` on a long text. Give its bench inputs whose results all add a multiple of 3 (`benches/members/README.md` § *Chain the inputs*). Rewrite `WRAP_DOC` in plain words. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:3277`, `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:3310`, `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:1328`

backlog: `Core\Str::lower` still builds a `String` through `str::to_lowercase` before its result, at most half as long again as the subject, to keep the final-sigma rule (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs` `nvs_core_str_upper`'s doc says so). Writing it through `built` needs the sigma rule restated.
Other `Core\Str` benches that chain with `% 3` may sit on one input too; each bench's word lengths decide it (`benches/members/README.md` § *Chain the inputs*).
